rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=12, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=123, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-11: ONE knob -> seed 42 -> 123, at the iter-10 val_n=12 PEAK basis (val_n=12/ep12/lr1e-4/warm_start True/n_iter600/grad_clip1.0). A CLEAN SECOND-SEED NOISE-FLOOR READ ON THE WIDER VAL BASIS (the handoff's explicit box-3 candidate). Everything else IDENTICAL to iter-10. DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-8 warm_start OFF dropped 0.5081->0.4486 (-0.0595, load-bearing-positive, settled); iter-9 lr 1e-4->2e-4 dropped 0.5081->0.4697 (-0.0384), so 1e-4 confirmed the per-scan step optimum at the converged init; iter-10 val_n 6->12 gave a wider-basis mean SSIM 0.4724 (hr 0.0038, PSNR 12.48) -- the new comparison basis. FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan (the 6-param bilateral twin physically cannot, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr~0); AND the per-image fit has a LARGE init-driven STOCHASTIC NOISE FLOOR -- a seed flip 42->123 at val_n=6 swung SSIM 0.5081->0.4203 (-0.088, iter-5 vs iter-7). That noise floor is the central obstacle to DOCUMENTING the ceiling (the iter-20 mandate): iter-10 widened the basis to val_n=12 (shrinking the per-scan standard error ~sqrt(2)) but read it at ONLY ONE SEED (42). Whether the ceiling is converged is still unanswerable from a single val_n=12 draw. EXHAUSTED axes (do NOT retry): n_iter (iter-2 1200 steps 0.4785->0.4293), warm_start (iter-8 off -0.06), lr (iter-3 1e-3->1e-4 + iter-9 1e-4->2e-4 bracket 1e-4 as optimal), pretrain_epochs (ep12 peak, ep18 worse 0.5016), unet_c (mayo n2i c16->c32 flat 0.9508, design-doc warned-against). grad_clip=1.0 is LOAD-BEARING (the 2304/128-view FBP-adjoint overflow guard, mandatory) -- and sweeping its VALUE is the OTHER untried candidate but LOW-VALUE here: raising it risks the adjoint overflow the guard exists to prevent and is not expected to move a ceiling -- so it is deliberately NOT chosen. LEVER CHOICE (box-3, genuinely untried, highest expected value toward iter-20): SEED 42 -> 123 AT THE val_n=12 BASIS. seed=123 was only ever run at val_n=6 (iter-7, 0.4203); pairing it with the wider val_n=12 basis directly measures how much of the documented stochastic noise floor SURVIVES the sqrt(2) averaging from doubling the val scenes. HYPOTHESIS: at val_n=12 the seed-42 (0.4724) and seed-123 reads land CLOSE (|delta| < ~0.03, much tighter than the val_n=6 0.088 single-seed swing), because averaging over 12 independent per-scan draws cancels most of the per-scan init stochasticity -> a trustworthy ~0.47-0.51 converged ceiling for the per-image U-Net N2I on this synthetic 128-view substrate. FALSIFIER: if the two val_n=12 seed reads STILL swing wide (|delta| > ~0.05), the stochastic floor is INTRINSIC to the per-scan N2I objective (not just init-set sampling) and that wide floor IS the documented ceiling finding -- the U-Net is structurally the wrong tool here vs the bilateral twin. hr expected ~0 either way (structurally FBP-bounded on dense 128-view phantoms). NOTE: this is a CEILING-DOCUMENTATION move toward the iter-20 mandate, not a ceiling-raising move; it pins down the variance of the wider-basis ceiling estimate. WALL: warm 12x200=2400 + per-image 12x600=7200 = 9600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 800 s (iter-10 ran in 914 s at this exact budget), under the outer_wall_s=1200 guard and the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall. All knobs IDENTICAL to iter-10 (train_n=200, val_n=12, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, lr=1e-4, unet_c=16, outer_wall_s=1200); ONLY seed 42 -> 123 changed.
